sonnet.problem: The statement quotes "for You are with me…", which is the right answer to card 9 ('Because the LORD is with him'). It re-asks the same fact in a different form. It also bundles several claims (the third-person lines, the quote, and the shift to addressing the LORD) and holds its own proof, so the baker has nothing to reason out.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The right answer is the verbatim Bible phrase 'For the sake of His name'. The wrong answers ('David's record', 'David's prayers') are plain invented phrasing, so the right one stands out as the one that sounds like Scripture.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
